circuits.name: XBOT NAND-2 (NOT-AND of 2 signals)
circuits.function: out = NOT(w2 AND w3); equivalently NAND of the two effective inputs (wires 2,3).
circuits.decode: eth_call to the processor contract with the calldata above (function eval(uint256,bytes), selector 0x934d06ea). The return is ABI-encoded bytes: offset (32B) + length (32B) + data. Data is 1 byte: 0x00 = output 0, 0x01 = output 1. Bit packing (verified on-chain): the `bits` argument is little-endian bytes; byte j bit k drives wire (8j+k+2). Wire 0 is constant 0 (GND) and wire 1 is constant 1 (VCC) — wire 1 = 1 was proven by two discriminating evals (ViperX circuits 2 and 3). Netlist format (verified): raw bytes from netlist(tokenId) are 7-byte records [type=0x00 (NAND)][in1: uint24 BE][in2: uint24 BE]; gate i outputs wire (n+i) where n = number of input wires (wires 0..n-1); the circuit output is the last gate's output. Simulate in JS: wires[0]=0, wires[1]=1, wires[2..n-1] from bits, then each gate wires[n+i] = NOT(wires[a] AND wires[b]). Example calldata uses bits=0x03 (w2=1,w3=1) so the expected output is 0.

circuits.name: XBOT Consensus 2-of-3 (Risk + Liquidity + Market)
circuits.function: out = 1 iff at least 2 of (Risk=w2, Liquidity=w3, Market=w4) are 1 (2-of-3 majority). Site's NAND network N1..N5,OUT reproduces the same function; the on-chain netlist appends a double-NOT buffer (gates 7-8) after OUT.

circuits.name: ViperX risk circuit #1 — leverage limit (value <= 2000, i.e. 20.00x)
circuits.function: out = 1 iff the 16-bit input value (wires 2..17, wire 2 = bit 0) is <= 2000. Interpreted as leverage in 0.01x units: 2000 = 20.00x, matching the docs' 'A trade above 20x is rejected on chain'.

Example calldata evaluates the threshold value itself, expected output 1.

notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-21 (block 76470149, chainId 196). All netlists were fetched live via netlist(tokenId); all truth tables / threshold rules were verified against on-chain eval(tokenId,bits): XBOT circuits 1 and 3 fully enumerated (16/16 and 32/32 eval calls, 0 mismatches vs the JS simulator); ViperX circuits verified by exhaustive simulation over caring wires + 20 on-chain threshold spot-checks (0 mismatches) + 2 discriminating evals proving wire 1 = constant 1. Total on-chain eval calls in this verification: 104 + 20 spot-checks + discriminating probes, 0 mismatches against the decoded netlist simulator. OKX Explorer could NOT be used from this VM (browser.open -> HTTP 403; explorer API endpoint returned empty) — contract source/ABI was NOT confirmed as verified on the explorer; the ABI above was recovered from deployed bytecode (selector extraction + 4byte.directory) and confirmed by live eth_call. Explorer links are included for manual checking. tapeout.net fetched 200 but returned only a 544-byte JS app shell (no processor list in text). TAPI-25 (community spec) lists netlist()/eval() as expected but normative ABI TODO — both functions exist on these contracts and the bit encoding was reverse-engineered here (little-endian bytes, byte j bit k -> wire 8j+k+2; wire 0 = 0, wire 1 = 1; gate i outputs wire n+i; output = last gate). ViperX circuit-name mapping: #1 = leverage is STRONG (threshold 2000 = 20.00x matches docs 'A trade above 20x is rejected on chain'); #2/#3/#4 = slippage/drawdown/cooldown in the docs' listed order is PLAUSIBLE but not individually proven (docs list the four names without per-ID mapping; thresholds are consistent: <=100 likely 1% slippage, <=156 drawdown, >=5 cooldown minimum). XBOT tokens 1,2 share one netlist (NAND-2); tokens 3,4,5 share one netlist (majority-3). The XBOT site calls circuit 3 'Circuit 3.2.268' (consensus). No adder, no latch, no multi-output circuit exists among these 6 distinct netlists — game levels must be built from the on-chain NAND primitive (functionally complete: AND/OR/XOR/NOT are compositions of NAND, verified against the on-chain NAND truth table), the on-chain majority gate, and the on-chain threshold gates. Do NOT claim an on-chain adder or latch. nextId() returns the circuit count, not the next token id. tokenURI() returns an empty string (no per-circuit on-chain metadata/names). Overclock circuits #5 (Game of Life) / #6 (CPU 4-bit) / #11 (neural net) were NOT included: their processor address is not published in the board page text. DeWEB/SiteRegistry addresses for X Layer were NOT verified (TapeKit SPEC is BNB-only); out of scope for this file. Factory cpuCount was 388 on 2026-10-23 (secondary source) and is 438 now — the ecosystem is growing; re-check cpuCount before submission.
